sibling_simulation.site: dfpn.rs mid(), after a defence is proved
sibling_simulation.guard: !attacking && value.proof == 0; sibling open and not already simulated
sibling_simulation.guide: the just-proved defence position, looked up in the proof table
sibling_simulation.budget: a fixed simulation counter per sibling
sibling_simulation.success: the sibling child becomes WON; the replay proofs are kept

simulate.attacker_move: the guide's stored proof move, or the guide's immediate explosion / dropped mate
simulate.defences: every legal reply; a reply that explodes the attacker fails, an exposing reply is a one-move proof, a stored proof is reused, else the same reply in the guide is replayed
simulate.cycle: the search path and the replay line are both checked

replay_threat.site: dfpn.rs mid(), defender node, no known value, not in check
replay_threat.null: pos.null(): side to move passed, en passant cleared
replay_threat.win: immediate explosion, a check every evasion loses, a double threat no defence parries, or a move into a known proof
replay_threat.replay: the null proof is replayed on every open defence via simulate()
replay_threat.miss: a fresh defence starts at half its proof number

sibling_simulation.guard: defender node, proved child, replay_exact or sim_exact
sibling_simulation.guide: the just-proved child position, looked up in the proof table
sibling_simulation.success: the sibling child becomes Proved; the replay proofs are stored and emitted

greedy_simulation.what: a bounded 6-ply greedy playout that adjusts fresh start numbers; no proof

null_replay.what: a 64-bit explosion-threat signature; parried/created only lowers the start pair via UNLIKELY
null_replay.null_position: never built; the signature is a pure function of the board

gaps.name: exact null-threat replay
gaps.provari: build the passed position, find a winning move, replay it on every open defence, lower a fresh parrying defence
gaps.atomi: signature-only prior; no null proof and no replay
gaps.portability: same DF-PN base and the same exact replay module; no new search algorithm

gaps.name: exposing one-move shortcut
gaps.provari: simulate_defences treats a defence after which the attacker can explode at once as a one-move proof
gaps.atomi: replay::simulate_defences had no such shortcut; it needed a stored proof or the guide's reply
gaps.portability: a local branch in guide/replay.rs using threat::immediate_explosion

gaps.name: guide explosion / dropped mate fallback
gaps.provari: simulate falls back to the guide's immediate explosion or dropped mate when the guide has no stored proof
gaps.atomi: simulate requires a stored guide proof
gaps.portability: local, but only useful once the null guide proof is supplied

gaps.name: top-level guide proof override
gaps.provari: the null proof is stored in the table and looked up like any other
gaps.atomi: the null position must not be keyed or stored, so the top guide move is passed explicitly

g2.rule: at least one concrete exactness gap portable without changing the DF-PN base
g2.verdict: G2-a..G2-d are portable on the existing DF-PN and replay base; Phase B is authorised

not_ported: provari's check-every-evasion and double-threat null-win cases (only the immediate explosion, stored proof and exposed mate-in-two are ported)
provari's recomputed proofs (atomi has no recomputed proof table)
